title: Bin El Ouidane reservoir on 26 Sep 2026
summary: On 26 Sep 2026 the radar shows a lake of 29.82 km2 inside the 10 km circle around Bin El Ouidane. Trees, shrub and rugged slopes cover 61.4% of the circle, and no flag applies to this date.

sections.heading: What the radar shows here
sections.text: The lake is the darkest surface in the circle: the open water type averages -18.17 dB in HH and -22.85 dB in HV, against a circle mean of -7.59 dB and -14.26 dB. That type covers 30.46 km2, a little more than the lake on this date, because it is drawn from the whole season.

sections.heading: Terrain types and what they mean
sections.text: Trees, shrub and rugged slopes have the brightest HV of the large types, -12.77 dB, because leaves and branches scatter the pulse in many directions. Rough dry ground and fields, 24.0%, give medium echoes from soil and stones. Built-up land is only 1.8%, but its HV:HH ratio of -13.63 dB is the lowest of all types, the double-bounce signature of walls.

sections.heading: Data quality notes
sections.text: The lake outline is approximate: 9.2% of it falls on land in the optical photo. Possible cause: radar shadow on steep shore slopes facing away from the single viewing direction. A shoreline survey or the dam's level record would check it.
